editorial:
Ever wondered how the women in the 007 movies changed over the decades? You get a front-row seat to that history here. The film brings together legendary stars like Ursula Andress and Jill St. John to talk about their time on set. It feels like a cozy chat with Hollywood royalty as you watch old clips from the early Bond epics. The vibe is light and nostalgic, focusing on how these women went from just being pretty faces to actually helping Bond save the world. It is a great way to see how movie roles for women shifted from the 1960s up through the early 2000s.

What really works is the pacing, as it jumps quickly between funny stories and surprising behind-the-scenes secrets. While it is not a high-action movie, the interviews keep you hooked because the ladies are so honest about their experiences. If you love movie trivia or just want to see some classic cinema, you should definitely check this out. You can grab it on a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or just look for it to rent on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by looking at the most modern Bond girls of the time. It shows that while the characters are still beautiful, they now have their own skills, like fighting or spying. The final scenes argue that the women became equals to Bond rather than just prizes to be won. It ends on a positive note, celebrating how these actresses broke barriers and paved the way for stronger female leads in action movies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves James Bond and movie history.
